components.title: Site secrets and PKI
components.description: OpenBao holding the site secrets, the PKI intermediate and the per-person keys.

control-implementations.description: What OpenBao's policies as code, its apply step, its rendered release and the site's signed evidence export show.

implemented-requirements.description: A session reaches only its own person's secrets and keys.

statements.description: OpenBao's session policies (deploy/openbao/policies) let a session token reach only its own person's paths: their KV secrets, their people directory entry (create and read only), their data-encryption key for making and unwrapping data keys, and a read of their own signing key. Every per-person path is templated on the OpenBao entity, no policy names a literal entity id, and no session path holds a wildcard under transit/. No session policy can list, export, back up, rotate, reconfigure, import, change or delete a key, and signing with the person's key is only in the step-up policy.
statements.remarks: Your organization runs the site's OpenBao from the policies as code and enrols each person's keys.

implemented-requirements.description: Moving a key needs two key custodians.

statements.description: Every OpenBao path that moves a key out or in (export, backup, restore, import and key configuration) is in the key-move policy behind a control group that needs two approvals from the key-custodians group; the install policy reaches only the static application secrets under kv/data/apps/, and the enrolment operator's policy reaches no KV path.
statements.remarks: Your organization names the key custodians and approves each key move.

implemented-requirements.description: OpenBao signs only after a fresh step-up.

statements.description: OpenBao's apply step gives the signing policy only to the step-up role, which accepts only a token whose acr is the site's step-up value and issues tokens that live no longer than the site's step-up window; both session roles accept only tokens for the sterling-sessions audience, take the person from the token's subject, and carry no default policy.
statements.remarks: Your organization sets the step-up value and window in the site file.

statements.description: The rendered OpenBao server configuration never turns TLS off and serves the openbao-tls certificate, which site-pki re-issues after the bootstrap CA's first one; its metrics listener serves metrics only and keeps the same certificate, and the site Prometheus reads it over HTTPS with the site CA. The agent injector and the CSI provider are off and no HashiCorp image is used.
statements.remarks: Your organization operates the site PKI.

implemented-requirements.description: OpenBao's seal is never a software token outside the lab.

statements.description: The site install's preflight refuses a site whose OpenBao seal uses the SoftHSM2 library, or whose render runs the lab's SoftHSM2 OpenBao image, unless the install runs in lab mode; a site file with no seal choice stops the render.
statements.remarks: Your organization supplies the HSM and its PKCS#11 library for a production site.

implemented-requirements.description: OpenBao keeps an audit device on.

statements.description: The rendered OpenBao server configuration enables a file audit device that writes to standard output, and Fluent Bit ships every container log to the site OpenSearch. On the running site, the signed evidence export counts OpenBao's enabled audit devices and its audit events in the last day.
statements.remarks: Your organization reviews OpenBao's audit records.

implemented-requirements.description: A sealed OpenBao or a failing audit device raises an alert.

statements.description: The site Prometheus raises an alert, with a severity, a summary and the review runbook, when OpenBao is sealed and when its audit device fails to write a request, and sends alerts to Alertmanager.
statements.remarks: Your organization names the people who receive the site's alerts.

control-implementations.description: Supply-chain statements generated from the component inventory. Do not edit by hand: run node compliance/src/cli.ts supply-chain-statements --write.

implemented-requirements.description: Generated from the component inventory: the component inventory lists its resources.

statements.description: The component inventory (compliance/resources.json) lists these resources for Site secrets and PKI, each with the pin the repository uses: image quay.io/openbao/openbao-ubi 2.7.3@sha256:bb94f6b1f1a3fbb7538d17d1c0509a13f1c2b382ebc1a67b99286b12c9628f71, chart openbao 0.30.8 (sha256:a1a202d6300de36b3be9d924d52ba7dd24c6a1c7cd5b660b9bbda975f725f02b) and tool kms-pkcs11 0.3.0 (sha256:c112c670e1bcca7a7b7625b13c0ecf1a43a62cd2651d29bf23befb2ad47c49bf). The compliance fit check over the whole repository, run as a CI test, fails when a resource the repository uses has no reviewed entry, or an entry lists a file that no longer uses it.
statements.remarks: Your organization keeps the inventory of what it installs at its site, with its owners, and reconciles it with this list.

implemented-requirements.description: Generated from the component inventory: the offline bundle import refuses a changed item.

statements.description: Before anything is copied to the site, the offline bundle import checks every item against the manifest your organization signed and refuses the bundle when an item is missing, extra or has another digest. For Site secrets and PKI that covers chart openbao 0.30.8 (sha256:a1a202d6300de36b3be9d924d52ba7dd24c6a1c7cd5b660b9bbda975f725f02b). A CI test of the import proves the refusal.
statements.remarks: Your organization builds and signs each bundle it approves with its own key, and imports only that bundle at its site.

implemented-requirements.description: Generated from the component inventory: its resources are reviewed and pinned before use.

statements.description: These resources of Site secrets and PKI each have a reviewed register entry with their licence, compliance fit and conditions, and are pinned as the component inventory lists them: image quay.io/openbao/openbao-ubi 2.7.3@sha256:bb94f6b1f1a3fbb7538d17d1c0509a13f1c2b382ebc1a67b99286b12c9628f71, chart openbao 0.30.8 (sha256:a1a202d6300de36b3be9d924d52ba7dd24c6a1c7cd5b660b9bbda975f725f02b) and tool kms-pkcs11 0.3.0 (sha256:c112c670e1bcca7a7b7625b13c0ecf1a43a62cd2651d29bf23befb2ad47c49bf). The compliance fit check over the whole repository, run as a CI test, fails when one of them has no reviewed entry, is marked as not fitting, or is an image without a sha256 digest or an action without a full commit SHA.
statements.remarks: Your organization selects and accepts its suppliers and runs its own supply-chain risk management plan.

implemented-requirements.description: Generated from the component inventory: the offline bundle import accepts only what your organization signed.

statements.description: The offline bundle import accepts a bundle only when its manifest verifies with your organization's public key and refuses a bundle signed with any other key, so these items of Site secrets and PKI reach the site only as your organization signed them: chart openbao 0.30.8 (sha256:a1a202d6300de36b3be9d924d52ba7dd24c6a1c7cd5b660b9bbda975f725f02b). A CI test of the import proves the refusal.
statements.remarks: Your organization keeps the signing key, signs only the releases it approves, and keeps its own record of each bundle it imports.
